title: Trump Called Netanyahu 'Crazy'—But Says They're Still Friends
summary: Did you ever get mad at a friend but still stay friends? That's kind of what happened between President Trump and Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In an interview on Wednesday, Trump said he called Netanyahu 'crazy' during a phone call. He was upset because Israel's fighting with a group called Hezbollah in Lebanon is making it harder to have peace talks with Iran. But Trump also said, 'I like Bibi a lot,' using Netanyahu's nickname. 'We've worked very well together.' Netanyahu agreed, saying they sometimes have 'tactical disagreements' but 'agree on the main things.' The fighting has been going on for months. Iran says any peace deal must also stop the fighting in Lebanon. Trump wants Iran to stop trying to build a nuclear weapon and to reopen a key waterway called the Strait of Hormuz so ships can carry oil again. The war has caused energy prices to go up, which worries many Americans. Meanwhile, the violence continues. On Wednesday, an Israeli strike hit a car on a busy highway in Lebanon, and Iranian drones hit an airport in Kuwait, killing one person. A fragile ceasefire—a temporary stop to fighting—has been in place since April, but both sides keep breaking it. So even though the two leaders say they're friends, the path to peace is still very bumpy.
why_it_matters: This conflict affects oil prices, which can make gas more expensive for families and raise the cost of everyday goods you use.

background_read: The U.S. and Iran have had tense relations for decades, especially over Iran's nuclear program. Israel and Hezbollah have fought many times over the years. President Trump (who took office in 2025) has tried to make peace deals in the Middle East, but conflicts often flare up. The Strait of Hormuz is a vital sea passage for oil, and when fighting disrupts it, energy prices around the world can rise.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu.
WHAT: Trump admitted calling Netanyahu 'crazy' but says they remain friends despite disagreements.
WHERE: The phone call connected the U.S. and Israel, while fighting occurred in Lebanon and an Iranian drone hit Kuwait.
WHY: Israel's fight with Hezbollah is hindering peace talks with Iran, and Trump wants Iran to stop its nuclear program and reopen a key waterway.

perspectives.description: They think it's okay for leaders to be honest with each other, and that calling someone 'crazy' shows they're close enough to speak freely.
They believe the disagreement is minor and that both leaders share the same goal of stopping Iran, so their friendship is strong.
They worry that name-calling makes peace harder and that both sides should focus on keeping the fragile ceasefire instead of blaming each other.
